question: Should Crabbox natively resolve Jujutsu revisions for synchronization, and if so should the supported contract be a Git-compatible export/ref workflow or a native jj revision/snapshot workflow?
rationale: The answer determines the core repository abstraction, expected revision identity, compatibility guarantees, and the scope of tests and documentation; source inspection does not establish a repository-approved contract.

options.title: Define a Git-compatible jj contract
options.body: Support jj repositories through a documented Git-export or reachable-ref workflow, preserving the existing Git-manifest model where possible.

options.title: Adopt native jj revision resolution
options.body: Add a first-class jj adapter that resolves jj revisions and snapshots independently of Git refs, accepting broader core surface and validation requirements.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Keep the current Git-only contract and document a supported external export/workaround until demand justifies a core abstraction.

recommendation.title: Define a Git-compatible jj contract
recommendation.body: Support jj repositories through a documented Git-export or reachable-ref workflow, preserving the existing Git-manifest model where possible.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a core-product boundary decision rather than a narrow regression repair.
